architecture.mechanism: Modular external steel structures with streamlined longitudinal high-low conical ribs and embedded micro serrations create geometric space constraints that physically block barnacle larval attachment and lateral expansion via narrow groove cavities and point-line contact surfaces.
architecture.intervention: Install the proposed steel structure system on the submerged hull and propeller surfaces of the 14,000 TEU container vessel without modifying the existing conventional antifouling paint coating.
architecture.expected_effect: The geometric constraints will prevent barnacle larvae from settling and establishing fouling colonies, thereby maintaining hull and propeller cleanliness between docking cycles.
architecture.falsification_test: Measure hull roughness and propeller performance at 6-month intervals using underwater drones and propeller torque sensors; if biofouling accumulation exceeds 5% of baseline drag or reduces propeller efficiency by more than 2%, the intervention fails.
